Early error-free arithmetic is due to M\o{}ller and Dekker~\cite{moller1965,dekker1971}. Priest and Shewchuk developed expansions and robust predicates~\cite{priest1991,shewchuk1997}. Later work studies 2Sum and Fast2Sum, verified renormalization, and double-word bounds~\cite{boldo2017twosum,boldo2017renorm,joldes2017,muller2022}; Park, Lim, and Nagarakatte broaden FastTwoSum conditions and give round-to-odd constructions~\cite{park2026}. FMA analysis, quad-double arithmetic, and extended- and mixed-precision BLAS provide related components~\cite{boldo2011fma,hida2001,li2002}, while MPFR and Arb provide reference arithmetic~\cite{fousse2007,johansson2017}. Our split~\eqref{eq:split} is semantic: Theorem~\ref{thm:alphabet} characterizes residual storage, not an instruction sequence.

Flocq, Coq integration, and Gappa formalize floating-point semantics and certified bounds~\cite{boldo2011flocq,melquiond2012,daumas2010,dedinechin2011}. Tiered SMT reasoning and source/execution caveats appear in~\cite{conchon2017,monniaux2008}; Stainless now handles a Scala subset with bit-accurate floating-point reasoning~\cite{gilot2026stainless}. FPTaylor and Daisy derive bounds or compile real specifications~\cite{solovyev2015,darulova2014}, whereas Precimonious and Herbie search precisions or rewrites~\cite{rubio2013,panchekha2015}. Relational domains include floating-point polyhedra, interval slopes, and TVPI~\cite{chen2008,chapoutot2010,rivera2024}; Z3, MathSAT5, cvc5, Bitwuzla, and abstraction-guided bit-blasting provide adjacent solving technology~\cite{demoura2008,cimatti2013,barbosa2022,niemetz2023,niemetz2024}. Proposition~\ref{prop:encoding} states only a fixed guarded QF-LIA encoding; the artifact runs no solver.

The lower bound is for one cell, point summaries, and Section~\ref{sec:separation}'s continuations. Composition assumes a finite relation, conservative acyclic wiring, a dyadic grid, guards, and representable residuals; generated tables are bound to one supplied network, not linked as untrusted contracts. The model identifies signed zeros and excludes NaNs, infinities, flags, overflow responses, flushing, implicit casts, arbitrary control flow, and target instructions. Toward-zero crossing zero needs a sign partition; full-alphabet storage may exceed reachable needs; joint phases can grow as $B^w$. The deterministic suites test conformance, not workload representativeness or performance---a large-scale study likewise finds that common benchmarks cover deployed floating-point structures only partially~\cite{gilot2026github}. Finite exactness is not a tractability, mechanization, or hardware claim.

Recent FPAN verification reduces sign, exponent, and bit-run abstractions to quantifier-free linear integer reasoning~\cite{zhang2025}. We ask a complementary question: for a fixed observation and allowed continuations, what information must a reusable module retain? This is an observation-relative problem in the sense of abstract-interpretation completeness~\cite{amato2011}, not a claim that one abstraction dominates another. It also differs from ordinary forward error analysis: a tight local bound can still forget which future error will cancel it.
